I'm getting this on v1.3.0 with agent-level permissions in `opencode.json`.

We hit the same issue downstream in dzianisv/opencode.

Our merged frontend mitigation is here: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/pull/57

That fix avoids sessions appearing permanently busy by only checking the last message in the UI instead of scanning older orphaned assistant messages.

While tracing the root cause, we found the backend can still leave assistant messages without  in crash/interruption paths (for example process shutdown or exceptions after stream setup), so the frontend fix is only a mitigation. A backend recovery/finalization fix is still needed upstream.

I hit a closely related real-world case while debugging : fresh  processes could recover after auth/account state changed on disk, but already-open sessions could stay stuck on stale provider state until restart.

I ended up fixing the plugin side with an OpenAI-style pattern very similar to this PR:
- reload latest provider/account state from disk at request time
- flush stale in-memory rate-limit/account-failure state
- retry once before hard-failing on stale  /  states

Upstream plugin PR for the concrete package-side fix: https://github.com/NoeFabris/opencode-antigravity-auth/pull/539

So from local repro: this core  direction is absolutely the right model for already-open sessions.

I hit a closely related real-world case while debugging `opencode-antigravity-auth`: fresh `opencode run` processes could recover after auth/account state changed on disk, but already-open sessions could stay stuck on stale provider state until restart.

I ended up fixing the plugin side with an OpenAI-style pattern very similar to this PR:
- reload latest provider/account state from disk at request time
- flush stale in-memory rate-limit/account-failure state
- retry once before hard-failing on stale `No Antigravity accounts...` / `All accounts rate-limited...` states

Upstream plugin PR for the concrete package-side fix: https://github.com/NoeFabris/opencode-antigravity-auth/pull/539

So from local repro: this core `reload + retry once` direction is absolutely the right model for already-open sessions.
